lines.japanese: 「ああもう、わかったから鳴らすな！」
lines.english: “All right, all right, I’m coming! Quit ringing the bell!”

lines.japanese: 「メリークリスマース！」
lines.english: “Merry Christmaaas!”

lines.japanese:
いきなり部屋を襲った大音響を迎え撃つべく
扉を開いたその先には、
さらなる大音響が待っていた。
lines.english: I opened the door to confront the sudden racket assaulting our apartment—and found an even greater racket waiting on the other side.

lines.japanese: 「……近所迷惑だから静かにしろ。早く入れ」
lines.english: “Keep it down. We have neighbors. Now get inside.”

lines.japanese: 「なんかノリ悪いな～」
lines.english: “Wow, way to kill the mood.”

lines.japanese: 「せっかくのクリスマスなのにね～」
lines.english: “And on Christmas, too.”
“Seriously.”

lines.japanese:
「さっきまでは悪くなかったよ。
……引っ越し前のクソ忙しいときに、
いきなり空気読まない招かれざる客が来るまではな！」
lines.english: “I was in a perfectly good mood until a bunch of uninvited guests barged in without a thought for how insanely busy we are right before a move!”

lines.japanese:
引っ越し間際で荷造りした荷物が積まれる中、
もともと二人でも手狭と言われる部屋に、今は５人……
lines.english: With packing boxes piled everywhere, there were now five of us crammed into an apartment already tight for two…

lines.japanese: ……まぁ、これで暖房は切っても問題なさそうだけど。
lines.english: well, at least we could turn off the heat.

lines.japanese: 「な～に言ってんだ、ちゃんと事前に連絡しただろ？」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? I gave you advance notice.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……今日の、しかも一時間前にな！」
lines.english: “Sure—today. An hour ago!”

lines.japanese:
武也からの緊急襲来警報を受け取ったとき、
俺も雪菜も、来客を迎える準備どころか、
帰宅すらしてなかった。
lines.english: When Takeya’s emergency invasion warning arrived, neither Setsuna nor I was even home, much less ready for company.

lines.japanese:
……まぁ、そのことに関して苦言を呈してるのは、
この家の中でも俺だけなんだけど。
lines.english: Though I was the only person in the apartment who seemed to have a problem with that.

lines.japanese: 何しろ、もう一方の住人の方は……
lines.english: The other resident, after all…

lines.japanese: 「雪菜～！　元気してた～？」
lines.english: “Setsunaaa! How’ve you been?”

lines.japanese:
「依緒～！　久しぶり～！
あれ、髪切った？　なんか昔に戻ってる～！」
lines.english: “Io! It’s been forever! Wait, did you cut your hair? You look like your old self again!”

lines.japanese: ほら、予想通り大はしゃぎだ。
lines.english: Sure enough, she was beside herself with excitement.
“Setsunaaa♪”

lines.japanese: 「あ～、あんたもいたんだ朋」
lines.english: “Oh. You’re here too, Tomo.”

lines.japanese: 「ひどいっ！？」
lines.english: “That is so mean!”

lines.japanese: 「え～、だってまだ月に一度は会ってるじゃない」
lines.english: “What? I still see you at least once a month.”

lines.japanese:
「今日はそれとはまた別じゃん？
仲間が一堂に会した時の違う感動とかあるじゃん！」
lines.english: “But today’s different! There’s a special feeling when the whole gang’s finally in one place again!”

lines.japanese:
ま、お互いここまで遠慮なく罵り合うのも、
まるで遠慮せず押し掛けてきやがるのも、
いつまでも仲がいいからということで……
lines.english: Well, the fact that they could insult each other this freely and that the others could come barging in here with just as little restraint was proof they were still as close as ever…

lines.japanese: 俺は許さないけど。このクソ忙しい時に……
lines.english: Not that I forgave them. Not when we were this busy…

lines.japanese:
「いや、来るなら今日しかないかなって。
明日は引越し前日だし、昨夜はイブだし。
……どうせお前らも昨日はベッタベタしてたんだろ？」
lines.english: “Today was really our only chance. Tomorrow’s the day before the move, and last night was Christmas Eve. You two were probably all over each other too, right?”

lines.japanese:
「やかましい。
昨夜は二人とも帰れなかったんだぞ？」
lines.english: “Shut up. Neither of us even made it home last night.”

lines.japanese: まぁ、ベッタベタしてないとは言わない。
lines.english: Not that we hadn’t been all over each other.

lines.japanese:
「うわぁ、やっぱマスコミ関係は大変だねぇ。
朋とか見てると全然そんなふうに感じないけど」
lines.english: “Wow. Media jobs really are brutal. You’d never guess from looking at Tomo.”

lines.japanese:
「白鳥は優雅に見えるその下で必死に足掻いてんのよ。
……こちとら年末年始休みないんだからね？」
lines.english: “A swan only looks graceful because you can’t see it paddling for dear life underneath. Some of us don’t get any kind of year-end or New Year’s break, you know.”

lines.japanese:
「そんなわけだから、
せめて新居に移って、落ち着いてから来て欲しかったぞ」
lines.english: “Exactly. So the least you could’ve done was wait until we’d moved and settled in.”

lines.japanese: 「どのくらいで落ち着くんだよ？」
lines.english: “How long is that going to take?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだな、半年くらい？」
lines.english: “Oh, I don’t know. Six months?”

lines.japanese: 「お前俺のこと嫌いなんだろそうなんだろ」
lines.english: “You hate me. You do, don’t you?”

lines.japanese:
まぁ、そんないつも通りの憎まれ口を叩きあいつつ、
それでも俺は、一つだけ武也の巧妙な叙述トリックを
見破った。
lines.english: We traded the same old abuse, but amid it all I caught one sly bit of narrative sleight of hand in Takeya's story.

lines.japanese:
「ね～ね～、鍋パーティやろうよ！
ちゃんと材料買ってきたからさ」
lines.english: “Come on, let’s have a hot-pot party! We even brought all the ingredients.”

lines.japanese: 「さっきメリークリスマスって言ってなかったか？」
lines.english: “Didn’t you just wish us a merry Christmas?”

lines.japanese:
「そんなこともあろうかと、
ちゃんと鶏鍋をチョイスしといたから～
メリークリスマース！」
lines.english: “We anticipated that objection, so we picked chicken hot pot! Merry Christmaaas!”

lines.japanese:
「鍋ならついさっき片づけて
今はその引っ越し荷物の山の中だ……」
lines.english: “I packed the pot away a few minutes ago. It’s somewhere in that mountain of boxes now…”

lines.japanese:
今さっき武也の奴、
お前ら“も”って言いやがった。
lines.english: A moment ago, Takeya had said, “You two were probably all over each other too.”

lines.japanese:
「雪菜、こっちの鶏煮えてるから……
白菜と豆腐も食べるだろ」
lines.english: “Setsuna, the chicken on this side’s ready. You want some cabbage and tofu too, right?”

lines.japanese: 「ありがと春希くん」
lines.english: “Thanks, Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「お、こっちのシメジの方も煮えてきたかな……」
lines.english: “Oh, these beech mushrooms look about done too…”

lines.japanese:
「それは俺が１分前に投入した奴だ。
２分ほど待て。
あと、それはシメジじゃない。平茸だ」
lines.english: “I put those in one minute ago. Give them another two. And they’re not beech mushrooms; they’re oyster mushrooms.”

lines.japanese: 「……相変わらず鬱陶しいねお前」
lines.english: “You really are as irritating as ever.”

lines.japanese:
「ほんっと、いつ来てもここの食卓は変わんないね～。
亭主仕切る仕切る」
lines.english: “Seriously, dinner here never changes. The husband still runs the whole show.”

lines.japanese:
「雪菜もよくこんなのと毎日顔突き合せてるよね～。
いい加減ウザくなってこない？」
lines.english: “Setsuna, how do you stand seeing this every single day? Doesn’t he ever get on your nerves?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、別に？
ウチで鍋やると重宝されるよ春希くん？
孝宏とか全部よそってもらってるし」
lines.english: “No, not really. You're a godsend whenever we have hot pot at my parents' place, Haruki. Takahiro has you serve him everything.”

lines.japanese:
「だってさ、孝宏君ほっといたら肉しか食わないんだぜ？
無理にでも野菜摂らせなきゃ」
lines.english: “Because if you leave Takahiro alone, he’ll eat nothing but meat. Somebody has to make him eat vegetables.”

lines.japanese:
「娘の旦那に食卓を支配されるとか、
それでいいのか小木曽家……」
lines.english: “The Ogisos let their son-in-law take over the entire dinner table… Is that family going to be all right?”

lines.japanese: 「しっかし、とうとうこの部屋ともおさらばか……」
lines.english: “So this is finally goodbye to the old place…”

lines.japanese: 「思い返してみると、やっぱり寂し……くもないわね」
lines.english: “Now that I think back on it, I guess I really am sad to see it… no. No, I’m not.”

lines.japanese: 「いつ遊びに来てもなんか説教されたし」
lines.english: “Every time I came over, I got lectured about something.”

lines.japanese: 「酒こぼしただけで怒られるし」
lines.english: “Spill one little drink and he gets mad.”

lines.japanese:
「そうそう、酔っぱらって吐きそうになったら
外に叩き出されるんだぜ？
ひっどい家主だよな～」
lines.english: “Exactly! If you get drunk and feel like you’re going to puke, he throws you out in the hall. Some host he is.”

lines.japanese:
「いやそれ、こっちの反応の方が当たり前だろ。
ていうか俺フォローしてたよな？
後かたずけも世話も全部俺がやってたよな？」
lines.english: “That's how anyone would react! And didn't I look after you? I cleaned everything up and took care of you every time, didn't I?”

lines.japanese:
「え～、そうだったっけ？
なんかいっつも帰り際に廊下を見ると、
武也が転がってたような……」
lines.english: “Really? I don’t remember that. I just remember that whenever I looked down the hall on my way out, Takeya was sprawled there…”

lines.japanese:
「お前はそうだった確かにお前はそうだったよ！
俺が潰れて苦しんでても一度も面倒見てくれなかった」
lines.english: “Oh, you were like that, all right! No matter how drunk and miserable I got, you never once looked after me!”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ、毎回潰れるほうが悪いだろ」
lines.english: “Anyone who gets that drunk every single time has only himself to blame.”

lines.japanese:
「しかも微妙に意識あるの隠してるのが
いやらしいんだよね～。
その場で仏心出したら何されるかわかったもんじゃない」
lines.english: “And the really creepy part was how he’d pretend to be out cold when he was still half-conscious. Show him one flicker of mercy, and God knows what he’d try.”

lines.japanese:
「仕方ないだろ！
だってあの頃はさ！」
lines.english: “What did you expect? I mean, back then—”

lines.japanese:
「ん～？　あの頃のあんたはどうだったって？
……あの頃のあたしは、どうだったって～？」
lines.english: “Hmm? What exactly were you like back then? …And what was I like back then?”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ、お前……あ」
lines.english: “Well, you were… oh.”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　なに？」
lines.english: “Hm? What?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、悪い、こっちだけで盛り上がっちゃって」
lines.english: “No, sorry. We got carried away reminiscing.”

lines.japanese: 「雪菜にはつまんない話だったよね～」
lines.english: “It must’ve been pretty boring for you, Setsuna.”

lines.japanese:
と、二人が盛り上がっていたはずの会話をぶった切り、
雪菜の方に少し申し訳なさそうな笑顔を向ける。
lines.english: And just like that, they cut short the conversation they'd been enjoying and gave Setsuna faintly apologetic smiles.

lines.japanese:
「わたしにも全然ついていけない話だったんだけど、
こっちへの謝罪は？」
lines.english: “I couldn’t follow any of it either. Where’s my apology?”

lines.japanese:
……まぁ、柳原についてはともかくとして、
俺には、二人が口を閉ざしてしまった理由が
痛いほどわかる。
lines.english: Never mind Yanagihara. I knew all too painfully why the other two had fallen silent.

lines.japanese:
だって今までの話題は、
ここが『雪菜の住処』となる前の話だったから。
lines.english: All those stories were from before this apartment became Setsuna's home.

lines.japanese:
俺が雪菜を遠ざけて、
武也と依緒と……あとごく少数くらいしか
この部屋の敷居を跨がなかった頃の話だったから。
lines.english: From the days when I kept her at arm’s length, and only Takeya, Io, and a tiny handful of others ever crossed my threshold.

lines.japanese: でも……
lines.english: But…

lines.japanese: 「ううん、聞かせて」
lines.english: “No. Tell me.”
“Setsuna…”

lines.japanese: 雪菜は、笑ってる。
lines.english: Setsuna was smiling.

lines.japanese:
あの頃の、悲しげで寂しげな笑顔じゃない。
無理めに感情を盛り上げた、
テンションの高い笑顔でもない。
lines.english: Not the sad, lonely smile she had worn back then. Nor the overbright, overexcited smile she had to work herself into.

lines.japanese:
「わたしの知らない春希くんを、
二人だけが知ってるのもなんか悔しいし」
lines.english: “Besides, it’s not fair that the two of you know a Haruki I don’t.”
“Setsuna…”

lines.japanese: だって、決めたから。
lines.english: Because we had made a decision.

lines.japanese: あの頃のこと、悪かった探しはもうしないって。
lines.english: We had decided not to go digging through those years for someone to blame.

lines.japanese:
過去の不幸を嘆くより、
これから幸せになることに全力を注ぐって。
lines.english: We would put everything we had into building a happy life from then on, rather than mourning the unhappiness in our past.

lines.japanese: そうやって、二人で決めたから。
lines.english: That was what we had decided together.

lines.japanese:
「それに、そういった情報の中に、
春希くんの弱みに付け込むヒントがあるかもしれないし」
lines.english: “And there might be something in those stories I can use against Haruki.”

lines.japanese: 「雪菜？」
lines.english: “Setsuna?”
“That’s terrifying!”

lines.japanese:
「雪菜、大人になった？
……ずいぶんと嫌な方向に」
lines.english: “You’ve really matured, Setsuna… in the worst possible way.”

lines.japanese: いや、決めたよな？　確か……
lines.english: Wait. We did agree to that, didn’t we? I was sure we had…

lines.japanese:
「ねぇねぇ、あの頃の春希くんの話、もっと聞かせてよ。
すっごく性格悪かったはずだよね？
なんか嫌な武勇伝とかないかな？」
lines.english: “Come on, tell me more about what Haruki was like back then. He must’ve been awful, right? Don’t you have any good horror stories?”

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、それは……」
lines.english: “N-no, that’s…”

lines.japanese:
「ちょっと～、そんなローカルな話より
わたしの話聞いてよ～」
lines.english: “Come on, enough with the private reminiscing. Listen to my stories!”

lines.japanese: 「それこそごく一部でしか盛り上がらない話でしょうが」
lines.english: “Your stories interest an even smaller audience.”

lines.japanese:
「まぁまぁそういうこと言わずに～。
東亜テレビのドロドロな内幕とか教えてあげるから～」
lines.english: “Oh, come on. I’ll tell you all the sordid secrets from inside Toua Television.”

lines.japanese:
「……それ盛り上がるかもしんないけど、
本当に喋っちゃっていいのか？」
lines.english: “That might be entertaining, but… are you sure you’re allowed to tell us any of it?”

lines.japanese:
「でさ、ちょっと込み入ったこと聞くけど、
お前ら、今どんな感じなんだ？」
lines.english: “So, this is kind of personal, but… where exactly do things stand with you two?”

lines.japanese:
ビールや酒もしこたま入り、
鍋も雑炊まで片づけた頃。
lines.english: By the time we’d drunk a heroic quantity of beer and sake and polished off the rice porridge at the end of the hot pot,

lines.japanese:
まぁ、自然の流れで、
俺たちは男子会と女子会に分かれてた。
lines.english: we had naturally split into the guys on one side and the women on the other.

lines.japanese: 「それがさ、すっごい勢いで冷戦中」
lines.english: “We’re in the middle of a raging cold war.”

lines.japanese: 「いや冷戦だったら冷え込むだろ、勢いないだろ」
lines.english: “How can a cold war rage? Shouldn’t things be cooling off?”

lines.japanese:
そうなると話題の中心は、
どうしたって俺たちのことよりも、
未だに決着のついていないもう一組の方に……
lines.english: That naturally made the other unresolved couple the focus instead of Setsuna and me:

lines.japanese:
俺たちよりも長い因縁を誇る、
中学時代からのめんどくさい二人の方の話になる訳で。
lines.english: the two pains in the neck whose tangled history stretched all the way back to middle school, even longer than ours.

lines.japanese:
「なんでそうなってんだ？
もう秒読みだと思ってたんだけど……」
lines.english: “How did that happen? I thought it was only a matter of time.”

lines.japanese: 「秒読みだよ、間違いなく」
lines.english: “It is. No question.”

lines.japanese: 「両親とかには会ったわけ？」
lines.english: “Have you met her parents?”

lines.japanese:
「会うも何も、中学の頃から
じいちゃんばあちゃん含めて全員顔見知り」
lines.english: “Met them? I’ve known the whole family since middle school, grandparents included.”

lines.japanese:
「そこで揉めたとか？
『こんなチャラチャラした奴に娘はやれん』とか」
lines.english: “So did they object? Say, ‘I’ll never give my daughter to a frivolous playboy like you’?”

lines.japanese:
「泣いて感謝されたよ。
俺の人当たりの良さをナメんな」
lines.english: “They wept with gratitude. Never underestimate my ability to charm people.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃあ、なんなんだよ？
まさかお前、また浮気……」
lines.english: “Then what is it? Don’t tell me you’ve been cheating again—”

lines.japanese:
「俺は、もうそういうことしないんだよ。
あとお前がそれを言うかお前が」
lines.english: “I don’t do that anymore. Also, you are the last man on earth who gets to say that. You.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええ？　なにそれ？」
lines.english: “W-wait, what?”

lines.japanese:
「だからさ……
子供ができたら、どっちが育児休暇取るかで喧嘩中」
lines.english: “Like I said… we’re fighting over which of us takes parental leave once we have a baby.”

lines.japanese:
「……いくらなんでも、
ちょっと先走りし過ぎじゃない？」
lines.english: “Isn’t that getting… just a little too far ahead of yourselves?”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう、そんなの結婚してから悩みなさいよ～」
lines.english: “Exactly. You can worry about that after you get married.”

lines.japanese:
「いやいや、そういうこと大事じゃん？
あたしさ、三年目になって、
だいぶ今の仕事の面白さわかってきたっていうか」
lines.english: “No, this stuff matters. I’m in my third year now, and I’m finally starting to see how interesting my job can be.”

lines.japanese: 「お局になって実権を手に入れただけじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Aren’t you just the office queen bee now that you’ve got some real power?”

lines.japanese:
「ま、まぁ、
ある意味リーダーシップが強いからね、依緒は」
lines.english: “W-well… Io has always had a certain gift for forceful leadership.”

lines.japanese:
「いやなってないから。
まぁ、そんなわけでさ、産休はともかく、
産んだ後は早めに復帰したいんだよね」
lines.english: “No, I’m not. Anyway, maternity leave is one thing, but once the baby’s born, I want to get back to work fairly soon.”
“Wow…”

lines.japanese:
「で、武也と半々で育休って訳に行かないかなって、
最大限譲歩しながら交渉してんだけど」
lines.english: “So I’m trying to negotiate a fifty-fifty split on parental leave with Takeya. That’s me compromising as far as humanly possible.”

lines.japanese: 「それ譲歩？　ねぇ、それ譲歩なの？」
lines.english: “That’s a compromise? You’re calling that a compromise?”

lines.japanese:
「難しいよね……
武也君も相当頑張ってるみたいだし」
lines.english: “It’s hard, though… Takeya seems to be working really hard at his career too.”

lines.japanese:
「そうなんだよねぇ……
悔しいけど、稼ぎも出世も向こうの方が上でさぁ」
lines.english: “Exactly. Much as I hate to admit it, he makes more money than I do, and he’s further up the ladder.”

lines.japanese: 「ならさ、しばらくは子供作んなきゃいいじゃん」
lines.english: “Then why not just hold off on having children for a while?”

lines.japanese: 「……それは嫌だ」
lines.english: “…I don’t want to.”

lines.japanese:
「やっぱ、子供は早めに欲しい。
こればっかりは二人とも同意見だ」
lines.english: “We both want kids sooner rather than later. On that much, we agree.”

lines.japanese: 「……そっか」
lines.english: “…I see.”

lines.japanese:
「な～んかそういうのって、
あなたたちのイメージじゃないけど」
lines.english: “That just… doesn’t seem like the two of you.”

lines.japanese:
「そっかな？
まぁ、そうかも」
lines.english: “You think? Well… maybe it doesn’t.”

lines.japanese:
「だいたいそれってさぁ、
もし別れちゃったら、子供が可哀想じゃない？」
lines.english: “Besides, what if you two split up? Wouldn’t that be awful for the child?”

lines.japanese:
「ううん、それは絶対にありえないよ。
……別れてしまうような関係なら、
１０年もかけて、ここまで辿り着いたりしない」
lines.english: “No. That will never happen. If ours were the kind of relationship that could end… we wouldn’t have spent ten years getting this far.”
“Io…”

lines.japanese:
「そこまで言い切れるくらいなら、
それこそさっさとくっついときゃ良かったのに」
lines.english: “If you can say that with such confidence, you should’ve just gotten together years ago.”

lines.japanese: 「……後悔しないか？」
lines.english: “You’re not going to regret it?”

lines.japanese: 「何言ってんだ、するわけないだろ！」
lines.english: “What are you talking about? Of course I’m not!”

lines.japanese:
「いや、そこまで青臭い話を俺に喋っちまったこと。
……俺なら明日頭抱えてるレベル」
lines.english: “I meant saying something that embarrassingly earnest to me. If it were me, I'd wake up tomorrow with my head in my hands.”

lines.japanese:
「……するに決まってんだろ。
絶対に『昨日言ったことは忘れろ』メール出すから」
lines.english: “Of course I’m going to regret that. I’m absolutely texting you tomorrow to say, ‘Forget everything I said yesterday.’”

lines.japanese: 「あは、あはは……」
lines.english: “Ha. Ha ha…”

lines.japanese: 人の想いは、どれも似たようなもので。
lines.english: The things people feel are all much alike.

lines.japanese:
けれど、一人一人微妙に違ってて、
そして、どれも、誰のも、かけがえのないもので。
lines.english: Yet each is subtly different, and every one of them—every feeling in every heart—is irreplaceable.

lines.japanese:
俺たちの事情も、
その近くで起こっていた事情も、
いつか時間と共に収束していく。
lines.english: What had happened to us, and what had unfolded in the lives around us, would all settle into place with time.

lines.japanese:
いつしか、良くも悪くも思い出に昇華され、
そして、良くも悪くも未来への道へと繋がっていく。
lines.english: Sooner or later, for better or worse, it would all be distilled into memory; and those memories, for better or worse, would lead on into the future.

lines.japanese: 「それじゃ、もう一度乾杯だな」
lines.english: “Then I guess that calls for another toast.”

lines.japanese: 「おう」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「お前たち二人に」
lines.english: “To the two of you.”

lines.japanese: 「お前たち二人に」
lines.english: “To the two of you.”

lines.japanese: 「あ～……柳原どうする？」
lines.english: “Uh… what about Yanagihara?”

lines.japanese:
「あいつはいいだろ。
俺たちが祝福しなくても、
勝手に幸せになるに決まってる」
lines.english: “She’ll be fine. With or without our blessing, she’s bound to go off and make herself happy.”

lines.japanese: 「……それもそうだな」
lines.english: “…True enough.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……乾杯」
lines.english: “Yeah… Cheers.”

lines.japanese:
だから、そんな先の見えない未来を祝福すべく、
俺たちは、また新しい缶ビールを口に運ぶ。
lines.english: And so, to celebrate that future none of us could see, we raised fresh cans of beer to our lips.
